note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old woman with ~1 week of dysuria, urinary frequency and suprapubic ache; reported pink-tinged urine today; clinician suspects acute uncomplicated cystitis and arranged urine testing and antibiotic treatment options.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Dysuria (burning/stinging with urination) for just under one week.
  - Increased urinary frequency interfering with university activities.
  - Suprapubic/low abdominal aching, worse with urination.
  - Noted pink-colored urine today (patient reports pink discoloration; likely hematuria).
- Timeline / progression:
  - Symptoms began just under one week ago; initially described as "a few days" then clarified to "just under a week."
  - Symptoms persistent, affecting daily activities; no clear improvement reported.
  - Conflict noted: clinician initially recorded "three days" then timeline was corrected by patient to "just under a week."
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Symptoms worse during and at the time of urination.
  - No specific relieving measures reported prior to consultation.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No fever reported.
  - No nausea or vomiting.
  - No flank or back pain.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge reported.
  - Bowel habit: background history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with variable stool consistency; bowel symptoms unchanged from baseline.
- Sexual and reproductive history:
  - Sexually active with a long-term boyfriend; typically do not use condoms.
  - Last unprotected intercourse approximately one week ago.
  - On combined oral contraceptive pill.
  - Last menstrual period two weeks ago.
  - Pregnancy status not tested or documented during visit; clinician noted to consider if symptoms persist.
- Substance use:
  - Tried cannabis once about 1.5 weeks ago (first time); does not smoke tobacco regularly.
  - Occasional social alcohol use.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) — patient-reported; symptoms variable, no new bowel symptoms.
- No history of bladder or kidney disease reported.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill — exact brand/type and dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Medication for IBS (patient stated name begins with "M"; exact medication name not documented), dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Reported adverse reaction to the antibiotic clindamycin; reaction described as "didn't go too well" (specific symptoms/reaction not documented).

Social History:
- Lives in university halls with a flatmate.
- Family live outside London; sees them occasionally.
- Student studying English at university.
- Cannabis: single use ~1.5 weeks ago; not a regular user.
- Alcohol: occasional social drinking.
- Tobacco: does not smoke.

Family History:
- No family history of bladder or kidney problems reported.
- No other relevant family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination performed or findings documented (clinician stated would not normally examine and did not examine on this occasion).

Investigations:
- Urine sample requested — patient to provide sample at clinic/practice drop-off; sample to be tested and sent to laboratory for analysis and culture. Results pending.
- No urine dipstick or microscopy results available in the record at time of consult.
- No pregnancy test performed or documented.
- No STI testing documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Probable acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection / cystitis
  - Assessment:
    - Clinical presentation consistent with lower urinary tract infection: dysuria, frequency, suprapubic ache, and recent pink discoloration of urine.
    - No systemic features to suggest upper tract involvement (no fever, vomiting, flank/back pain).
  - Plan:
    - Arrange urine sample for laboratory testing (dip/culture) — patient to drop off sample at practice.
    - Empiric antibiotic therapy offered; options discussed: trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin (nitrofurantoin described as a three-day course). Exact antibiotic choice, dose, route, and frequency not documented.
    - Advise adequate oral hydration.
    - Recommend simple analgesia (paracetamol) for pain as needed.
    - Safety-netting: return or contact clinician if development of fever, back/flank pain, vomiting, or if symptoms do not improve within one week.
    - Lab will inform patient of urine culture results and antibiotic sensitivities; antibiotic regimen to be adjusted if culture indicates alternative therapy.
- Issue 2: Contraception / pregnancy consideration
  - Assessment:
    - On combined oral contraceptive pill; had unprotected sex approximately one week ago.
    - Pregnancy not excluded or tested during visit.
  - Plan:
    - Clinician noted to consider pregnancy if symptoms persist; no pregnancy test ordered at time of consult (patient instructed to follow up if concerns).
- Issue 3: IBS (baseline)
  - Assessment:
    - Chronic IBS symptoms described; current bowel symptoms unchanged from baseline and not felt to be related to presenting urinary symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - No changes to IBS management documented.
- General plan items:
  - Counselled regarding avoidance of regular cannabis/tobacco use for general health.
  - Follow-up arranged: patient to return if no improvement within one week or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure) not documented.
  - Physical examination of abdomen and external genitalia/pelvic exam not performed or documented.
  - Immediate urine dipstick/microscopy results not provided.
  - Exact antibiotic selected, with dose/route/frequency, not documented.
  - Pregnancy test and STI testing were not performed or documented; may be clinically relevant given unprotected sex.
  - Exact name and dose of IBS medication unclear; medication name not documented.
  - Specific details of the clindamycin reaction not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Timeline conflict: clinician initially noted symptoms for "three days" then patient clarified "just under a week" — patient timeline clarified to just under one week; conflict noted.
  - Medication name for IBS uncertain (patient only stated it begins with "M"); exact medication not specified — conflict/uncertainty noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Transcript largely intelligible and adequate for clinical documentation.
  - Some details unclear or indistinct in transcript (exact IBS medication name; specifics of past antibiotic adverse reaction).
